newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela gas project needs 10 pct return--Giusti.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela gas project needs 10 pct return--Giusti.

text.p: An ambitious natural gas project between Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) Royal Dutch Shell, Exxon Corp and Mitsubishi Corp will need to show at least a 10 percent return on investment if it is to go ahead, PDVSA President Luis Giusti said Wednesday.
"PDVSA has a policy that the minimum rate of return must be 10 percent. Everything is measured against this level of profitability," Giusti told a news conference with foreign correspondents.
A final decision on the Cristobal Colon project, located off Venezuela's northeastern Caribbean coast, will be taken in December, Giusti added.
Weaker than expected natural gas prices have forced the revision of the project's scale from $5.7 billion to $4.5 billion.
Initial estimates saw the massive offshore find producing 140,000 barrels equivalent of liquid natural gas per day.
Exxon, Shell, Mitsubishi and PDVSA unit Lagoven signed a closing agreement in June transferring operations of the Cristobal Colon project to the joint venture company Sucre Gas SA.
Sucre Gas is owned 33 percent by PDVSA unit Lagoven, 30 percent by Shell, 29 percent by Exxon and eight percent by Mitsubishi.
